FILE t_lun.wav:
lun00 (0.0-5.5s): "Perilunate and lunate dislocations are easy to miss, and both are emergencies."
lun01 (7.0-12.4s): "They follow a high energy fall onto an outstretched hand, with the wrist bent back."
lun02 (13.9-23.8s): "On a normal lateral view, three bones stack in a straight line. The radius, then the lunate sitting on it like a cup, then the capitate sitting in the lunate."
lun03 (25.3-33.3s): "In a perilunate dislocation, the lunate stays in place on the radius. But the capitate, and the rest of the carpus, dislocate, usually dorsally."
lun04 (34.8-44.5s): "In a lunate dislocation, the lunate itself is pushed out toward the palm, and tips forward. That's the spilled teacup sign. The capitate drops back in line with the radius."
lun05 (46.0-52.2s): "On the frontal view, the smooth carpal arcs are broken, and the lunate looks triangular, like a slice of pie."
lun06 (53.7-59.5s): "Always look for an associated fracture. The scaphoid waist is the most common."
lun07 (61.0-66.7s): "The median nerve is at risk in the carpal tunnel, especially with a lunate dislocation."
lun08 (68.2-72.6s): "Both need urgent reduction, and usually surgical repair."
lun09 (74.1-82.1s): "Check the lateral view. Radius, lunate, capitate. If the line is broken, find which bone has moved."
Key words: perilunate (perry-LOO-nate); lunate (LOO-nate); capitate (CAP-ih-tate); carpus; dorsally; scaphoid (SKAF-oyd); median nerve; carpal

tolosa02 (21.0-24.8s): "Granulomatous inflammation there squeezes those nerves."
tolosa08 (26.3-30.2s): "So a follow-up MRI is needed to confirm that it resolves."
tolosa09 (31.7-38.8s): "Painful ophthalmoplegia, and an enhancing cavernous sinus? Think Tolosa-Hunt, after excluding the rest."
